Migrating them is the wrong fix — 56 of the 71 are custom property definitions, and relative colour there needs an `@supports` block per pack, which is machinery in the file a reader is told to copy verbatim. The right fix is cheaper: each literal states its source (`/* = --on-ink at 72% */`, which `ledger`'s eighteen now do) and a check recomputes the declared relationship, so a token that moves fails in CI instead of drifting silently. 47 comments, derived not chosen, then one check.

A typed custom property validates its own value — an invalid one becomes the declared `initial-value` instead of an inherited surprise — and is animatable, which is what a colour or a length token usually wants. The cost is the reason it is filed rather than done: the token layers are files a reader is told to copy verbatim, and a `@property` block per token would roughly double them. The narrow version worth pricing first is the handful of tokens that are actually animated (the accent, the elevation, the durations) rather than all of them — and that list has to be measured from the kits' transitions, not guessed.

Not one sweep and not a token per pack either: prose that states the sizes satisfies the bar as well as a token does, and which of the two is right depends on whether the pack's reference can still be read. What actually stays open is the umbrella and the family members that ship JS suites, where the same collision is available and unchecked. The commit message had this right and the row, which is what the next run reads, did not.

**58 palette-table rows name a surface other than the base their header declares, and the difference between the ordinary case and a wrong number is not mechanically decidable.** Measured 2026-08-20 while closing B-047, and filed rather than gated *because the broad check was tried and rejected*: in nearly all 58 the row's SUBJECT is a surface token, correctly measured on the declared base, and a gate that flags those teaches an agent to route around it. Only a row that **confines** its token to another surface is wrong, and `validate_confined_tokens_measured_where_used` catches exactly that — with **zero** live subjects after the scoreboard fix, so it ships as a regression guard with a plant rather than as a measurement. What stays open is the other direction: a row whose confinement is stated in prose ELSEWHERE in the pack rather than in the cell, which no pattern in the cell can see. The cheap partial fix is a `Measured on` column wherever a table's rows do not share one base — 47 base-declaring tables exist and one has it.

The checkable shape is narrow and worth pricing: for each duration token, collect the element words in the CSS comment and in the prose sentence naming the same token, and refuse a pair that falls in two different bands. The corpus is 112 duration declarations.

**Thirty-four run stamps will never carry a `Diverged?` answer, and nothing marks the boundary where the record becomes trustworthy.** Measured 2026-08-20 while closing B-051: the answer is not derivable (0 of 34 rows have their commit named in the Log), so those rows are permanently blind and archaeology would be invention. The related open question is whether the third trigger should read a window of five at all when 34 of 57 rows cannot answer; five was chosen when the table was short, not measured.

Fix shape: name all four proof-depth axes in the `Cost:` line that stages 3 and 4 already require, and define one abbreviated route whose floor is stated rather than implied. **Citation re-pointed 2026-08-20.** It cited "`gates.md:465-474`" and "`gates.md:488-493`"; both passages are at the addresses this row now carries. **Five of the eight useful measurements are not computed, and every one is two greps from data already on disk.** Only `unlooked`/`abstained` is genuinely computed. **Reopened gates**: `templates/run.md` writes a timestamped `stage:` line on every gate return and `templates/stage-coverage.sh` throws them away by design, keeping only the last verdict. **Time from implementation-complete to accepted**: same lines, same timestamps, no consumer reads them. **False-green incidents**: the class is named with five known shapes and counted nowhere, in a pack whose thesis is that green must be earned. **Manual proof fields still needing automation**: `review` is deliberately excluded from every per-run bucket because it would print the same standing number — correct per run, and exactly why the manifesto lists it as a **system** measurement; the population is already enumerable from the propagation matrix's `review` cells. **Requirements with no evidence path**: enforced per run as a gate and never counted. Invalidated proofs is B-081; do not duplicate.

**The walking skeleton is one unfalsifiable sentence on a path most work never takes.** `references/decomposition.md:57-60` calls the first module *«the thinnest end-to-end slice that proves the architecture»* and gates it with an escape written in. **The enforcement ladder tops out at a control that fails open, and has no rung for a capability boundary.** `references/gates.md:128-132` ranks five mechanisms — doctrine line, review question, script check, CI step, hook, the fourth promoted when *«it must hold for people who never run it locally»* — and the top rung is a Claude-Code-only hook that the same file records as **failing open** on a crash. The manifesto's strongest control is of a different kind: not a check that decides, but a capability the run does not hold. Everything outward this pack protects — deploy, publish, opening a PR, creating a shared design file — is guarded by prose plus a manual gate, and both are exactly what a context loss removes, which is the case the manifesto's example is chosen to survive. Fix shape: a sixth rung, *capability boundary*, defined as «the action is impossible because the credential, scope or network path is absent», plus a stage-0 autonomy row asking which credentials this run's environment actually holds and which the operator wants withheld; promote to it when a rule protects an irreversible outward act. This is also the honest answer to why the grill needs a hard floor at all — a floor is what you build when the fence is prose. **Citation re-pointed 2026-08-20.** It cited "`gates.md:61-78`", which is the judgment-gate section; the ladder is at the address this row now carries. The address resolved and pointed at other text, which is the failure a resolving address cannot report on its own; the row now quotes the phrase it points at, and `test/validate.py` resolves every `file:N-M` in an **open** row against that quote. **No evidence row records where or when the check was observed.** The coverage table's columns are REQ, Requirement, Status, Evidence; the verification ledger carries `Shipped in` and nothing about the environment the check ran in or the time it was observed. A smoke test against a preview URL therefore enters the record in a shape indistinguishable from one against production, and a suite that passed on a laptop with accumulated state is indistinguishable from one that passed on a clean runner. This pack already owns the incident the field exists for: `references/learned.md:136` records a suite green on every author's machine and 1039 failures on a runner that started clean. The lesson was written down and the field was never added. Combined with B-086, the pipeline instruments two of the five members of a proof's validity domain — commit-ish and, partially, time — and silently drops the rest. Fix shape: environment as a required cell on every evidence row, drawn from the vocabulary the project's own runbook declares; stage 8 refuses to write a verification row whose observation names a non-production target while the REQ claims production behaviour. **The environment half closed 2026-08-20:** `Environment` is a required cell on every row of `templates/verification.md` and of this project's own ledger, with the vocabulary declared in the template — `production` · `preview` · `ci` · `local` · `—` — and read from there by `test/validate.py`, never listed in the checker. `—` is a **recorded absence**, the same shape `Observed at` was introduced with, and every row predating the column carries it; an **omitted cell** is refused, because a row that forgot the question is not a row answering it. **A member can ship a coordination config whose generated snapshot is stale, and only the PARENT's CI notices.** Observed 2026-08-17 while releasing: B-065 added `SKILL-CARD.md` and `docs/evidence/specs/*carryover*.md` to `guardedFiles`, `docs/AGENT_SYNC.md` was not regenerated, and **`npm test` here stayed green through the whole release** — v1.69.0 was tagged, published to npm and smoke-tested with the snapshot already stale. The asymmetry is the defect: the check exists once, in the parent, for a config that lives in the member — so a member's own gate cannot refuse a change the member made. `CLAUDE.md` already states the rule (*if the two disagree the tool is right and the file is stale, regenerate rather than edit*) and nothing here enforces it. Fix shape: `test/validate.py` runs `agent_sync.py check` where `.claude/agent-sync.json` exists, disclosing a skip when the tool is absent rather than passing silently — the parent's copy then becomes a second opinion instead of the only one.

**A release checks out the tag to pin it, and the next commit lands on a detached HEAD.** Done here 2026-08-17: pinning the umbrella at the tag's own tree required `git checkout v1.69.0` in the submodule, and the coordination fix committed after it went onto a commit whose parent was the **tag**, not `main` — orphaning it from the two rows already on the branch. The shape is worth a mechanism because the sequence that causes it is the CORRECT one — pinning the tag's tree rather than the branch tip is what `skills.json`'s version claim requires, so this will recur every release. Fix shape: the parent's release procedure returns the submodule to its branch immediately after staging the pointer (`git -C <dir> checkout main`), because the pointer is already recorded in the index and the working checkout no longer matters; and a member-side guard refuses a commit made on a detached HEAD unless the message says why.

**Fourteen consecutive releases carry no run stamp, and the cold-retirement trigger has had nothing to read across all of them.** Measured 2026-08-20 by tag range rather than by grepping a tag's own commit — a stamp names the commit the *run* ended on, never the release commit, which is why the receipt in `retro.md` reported every tag as unstamped as written: `v1.60.1` through `v1.72.0`, 14 of 117 tags, and 84 unstamped overall because the register began at `v1.41.0`. Fix shape: run the pipeline on this repository again, or state a policy for guard-only releases and give the cold trigger a second countable unit that such a release moves.

**Two of the registered claim classes match their noun anywhere, so they only worked while the corpus never narrated.** `negative self-tests` matches any `N guards` and `gates.md's own axes` any `N axes`. Bringing the registers into the corpus on 2026-08-20 refused 26 statements and every one was narration — "Two guards caught the change as it landed", "1, 2, 3 and 4 guards not firing", "two axes of four". The dated-record exemption removed most of them and the rest were reworded with a qualifier between the number and the noun, which is the device the `rotation axes` class already relies on. Both were caught by the gate rather than by review, which is the arrangement working and also the measure of how often the rule will be broken. Fix shape: split each class into a total form and a subset form so the subset can be recognised rather than avoided.

**The widened reference-file class reads three phrasings, and a fourth was in the bundle.** `references/progress.md` said *«over 34 files nobody checked»* against a directory of 35 — found by grep while fixing the three surfaces the class does catch, not by the class. The pattern now covers `N reference files`, `N doctrine files` and ``N files under `references/` ``; a bare `N files` is deliberately outside it, because in this corpus that phrase counts guards, surfaces, plants and fixtures far more often than reference files, and a class that fires on all of them is a class somebody switches off. Fix shape: give the bundle's size one name the doctrine actually uses and check that instead of enumerating phrasings — the same move `_axis_keys()` made for the rotation axes.

**The citation-currency guard reads open rows only, so every closed row's `file:N-M` is unchecked forever.** 9 spans are checked and 6 single-line citations are disclosed as unanchored; the 5 ranges in closed rows are neither. That is deliberate — a closed row states what was true at closing, and rewriting it edits a record — but it means the `## Closed` list and every closed row's evidence can rot into pointing at other text with nothing saying so. Fix shape: resolve a closed row's citation against the commit its State cell names rather than against `HEAD`, which is the only comparison that is both checkable and honest.

**Three surfaces state three different rules for what the retro archive receives.** `references/retrospective.md` says the Recent log is **uncapped by design** and the run stamps are capped at ten with rotation at the eleventh. `cursor/rules/task-pipeline.mdc` says *«Entries older than the last five run stamps move to an append-only archive»*, and `docs/evidence/retro/2026-Q3.md` says its entries were rotated *«once they fell outside the last five run stamps»* — a window for log entries that the doctrine does not have and nothing enforces. Found 2026-08-20 while collapsing `B-060`/`B-069`: fixing the live heading exposed that the false bound also lives in a self-contained Cursor rule and in the archive's own header, and choosing between *uncapped* and *five stamps* is a doctrine decision, not an edit — so it was filed rather than taken. **The three tiers are dispatched by instruction, and nothing checks that a run actually dispatched three.** `certify` refuses a certification that arrives with fewer than three reports, which is the half that can be mechanised — but a run may still close a node by writing one verdict by hand and calling `close --verdict` directly, which is the path `verifier.md` deliberately still documents for a verdict already in flight. So the gate is complete and the OBLIGATION to use it is doctrine. What would close this: `close` refusing a verdict for a node whose `certification.round` is absent, with a named escape for the in-flight case. Filed rather than done because that flag is a migration for any graph mid-run when it lands, and this release already changes how every node closes.

**The run receipt records no cost, no retries and no human-corrections count** (extends B-096). Anthropic publishes per-phase cost tables for its own long-running harness — planner $0.46, build $113.85, QA $10.39 (*Harness design for long-running agents*, anthropic.com/engineering, read 2026-08-30) — and the harness-engineering digest's Change Receipt carries `cost_usd`, `retries` and `human_corrections` per change. This pipeline records none of the three: grep finds only a qualitative "token cost" (certification.md, *What this costs*). Fix shape: optional computed fields on the run ledger / hand-back — cost per stage where the harness exposes it, retry count from the `touch:` lines it already keeps, human corrections from the manual-gate returns — disclosures, never targets.

**Stage 6's evidence channels are code- and UI-shaped, and research/data deliverables have no named channel** (extends B-074). The gate doctrine names tests for code and the browser look for UI; a RESEARCH deliverable (a market summary, a doc synthesis) and a DATA deliverable (a migration, a dataset) reach stage 6 with no stated channel, so their verification is whatever the run improvises. External framing agrees: the digest's per-artifact-class table is CODE→tests, UI→render+screenshot, RESEARCH→sources+contradiction check, DATA→schema+range+freshness (read 2026-08-30). Fix shape: a per-artifact-class evidence-channel table in gates.md, and verification.md rows naming the channel used.

**Nothing computes which harness clauses were born under which model generation.** The doctrine now says to re-test compensating controls when the confirmed tier moves a generation (model-tiering.md → *A harness clause encodes a model's weakness*, shipped v1.80.0), and no mechanism lists the clauses or their birth generations, so the re-test is a memory. Fix shape: a dated `born-under` note on caps and ceilings (fix-loop 5, certify ceiling 3, the context-budget flush point), and a checkup line naming clauses older than the current generation.

**The failure mode where a model prematurely wraps up as the window fills has no name in the continuity doctrine.** Anthropic names it "context anxiety" — the model starts summarising and closing early when it believes the window is nearly spent, even when it is not (read 2026-08-30). continuity.md's Part 2 already forbids declaring the context exhausted without a signal, which is the same failure from the other side; naming it beside the boundary doctrine gives run reviews a word for what they are seeing. Fix shape: one paragraph in continuity.md → Part 2 (and the hand-back's NOT VERIFIED note where a run wrapped early), citing the dated source.

**On the cheapest tier, checkup/setup/prod-check phrasings route to project-audit instead of task-pipeline's own modes.** Measured 2026-08-31 in the blind trigger probes (evals/RESULTS.md → the haiku run): «что у нас накопилось непроверенного?» (TRIG-05, the checkup trigger), «проверь документацию проекта перед тем как что-то строить» (TRIG-06, setup) and «проверь, всё ли живо в проде после вчерашнего релиза» (TRIG-09, production check) all answered `project-audit`; sonnet and opus routed all three correctly. The two skills now genuinely share the what-is-unverified ground and only the fuller descriptions separate them. Fix shape: name the seam in both descriptions — project-audit's Not-for gains "what shipped unverified is the pipeline's checkup", task-pipeline's checkup clause names its own two modes harder — and keep TRIG-05/06/09 as the eval anchors that must stay green.

**The validator accepts a guard-count form the CI plant cannot land on, so a release passes locally and fails in CI on formatting.** `validate.py` reads `Guards: N → M` with the second number optionally bold; the negative self-test in `validate.yml` first probes that same loose pattern to decide whether to INJECT a count, then mutates with a strict one requiring `→ **M**`. A count written without the bold satisfies the loose probe — so nothing is injected — and then fails the strict search with `PLANT DID NOT LAND: no guard count in the TOPMOST section`. Observed 2026-09-01 on `fix/b119-dupids`: `npm test` → `rc=0` locally, CI red. The class is this repository's own recurring one — the check that ran was not the check that mattered — and here the two checks are a local gate and its own CI plant disagreeing about a format neither documents. Wanted: one pattern, defined once and read by both, or a `validate.py` refusal when the count is present in a form the plant cannot mutate.

**A release here is two merges whose ORDER is load-bearing, and nothing checks it until the tag exists — three tags burned in one day.** A run stamp must cite a commit inside the new tag's OWN range, and that commit does not exist until the payload merges, because the ruleset rebase-merges and mints every SHA at merge time. So the protocol is: payload lands as `X`, a SECOND change stamps the run citing `X` and lands as `Y`, tag `Y`. Cut the tag on `X` and the release is unstamped. `validate.yml` ignores tag pushes and `release.yml` is the first thing to run on the tag's own tree, so the branch is green either way and the cost is always a burned version — the ruleset forbids deleting a tag. Paid three times on 2026-09-01: `v1.82.0` (stamp written in the sibling repo's bullet shape into a section this gate reads as a table), `v1.82.1` and `v1.82.2` (tag cut on the payload commit, no stamp for the release's own run) — the third by the run that had just written the rule into the CHANGELOG. Wanted: something that refuses BEFORE the tag — a `release:preflight` script that resolves the range the tag would create and asserts a stamp falls inside it, run by the release checklist and by `validate.yml` against the version in `package.json`. **A fourth mechanism, 2026-09-01:** `v1.82.3`'s stamp was correct and in the right order, and the release still failed — on a negative self-test added in the same programme. `test/negatives.py` locates a plant's scratch directory by searching its script for a literal `cp -R . <dir>`, then diffs that copy against the repository to tell a real defect from a no-op; the duplicate-id plant copied ONE file and mutated the live tree, so the harness could not confirm it landed and reported the guard as one that did not fire. `npm test` cannot see this, because `negatives.py` is a CI step and not part of the suite. So the preflight this row asks for must run the PLANT HARNESS as well, not only `npm test` — four dead tags, four different mechanisms, one shared shape: a green local gate that does not cover what the release runs. **A fifth instance, 2026-09-02 — caught before the tag was pushed, and the first one that cost nothing.** The repair for `v1.82.3` was green on all three branch checks and would have burned `v1.82.4` on the release-gap check: it declared no stamp for the release it was itself creating. A PR repairing burn N is STRUCTURALLY blind to burn N+1, because the check lives on a tree the branch never has. What caught it was cutting the tag locally and running `npm run test:all` in a worktree at the tag, then deleting the tag on the failure — so the preflight this row asks for already exists as `test:all`, and what is missing is not a new check but running the existing one on the tag's own tree. `npm test` is three of its thirteen.

**19 live execution packets still carry the bare `execution-packet/1` id.** 1.93.0 namespaces the id (`task-pipeline/execution-packet/1`) and still reads the bare one. Counted 2026-10-12: `grep -l '"schema_version": *"execution-packet/1"' passioncode-platform/.task-pipeline/packets/*.json` → 19 (other repositories under `~/DATA`: 0 at that depth). Migrate them (rewrite `schema_version`, re-hash where the packet is content-addressed) or keep reading the bare id; only then refuse it.
